propositions: An AST gate must detect six categories of prohibited config/credential reads (ambient env, helper-shim env, load_config, literal-getattr env, provider-credential, configurable defaults/backend reload) in non-approved seam modules, reusing gen_env_registry's scanner and shim-resolution logic as a single source.

Approved composition-root and provider-credential-boundary seams must be enumerated distinctly; owner sets for credentials and env names must be derived at runtime from _child_env, _ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES, and static @register decorator scans, not hand-copied or inferred from import-time-empty registries.

Receiver-object aliasing (e.g., src = os.environ; src.get('SECRET')) and callee aliasing (import/local bindings) must be resolved to detect evasive reads; dynamic env-name args and shim-shaped callees absent from KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS must fail closed as unresolved-env-read.

A legacy-exception set with exact path+symbol+rationale entries must cover current below-seam reads so the gate is introducible without product-code changes; path-glob exceptions must be rejected structurally, and newly declared env names lacking an owner must fail (drift self-test).

The gate must expose check(root)->list[str] and main(argv)->int contracts mirroring check_config_reads.py, run offline with no network/CI dependency, exit 0 on the current tree, and include synthetic fixtures for all six categories in direct/import/local-aliased forms plus clean approved fixtures.
Self-tests must validate that a new bypass, unowned credential/env name, path-glob exception, or missing rationale each fail; the unresolved-env-read case (dynamic or absent shim) must fail closed.
